claims.text: The baseline is a single-phase refractory high-entropy alloy optimized for low density and room-temperature performance.
The baseline alloy contains no engineered second-phase precipitates.
Adding 0.5–1.0 wt% yttrium during processing will induce in situ formation of Y2O3 precipitates.
The intervention will produce stable, uniformly dispersed, nanometer-scale Y2O3 precipitates.
Nanoscale oxide particles will pin dislocations at elevated temperatures.
Nanoscale oxide particles will pin grain boundaries at elevated temperatures.
Dislocation and grain-boundary pinning will mitigate high-temperature creep and softening.
A low oxide volume fraction will preserve room-temperature ductility and strength.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will improve high-temperature yield strength or creep resistance by approximately 10–20% relative to the alloy without the addition.
The intervention will cause only minimal changes in room-temperature mechanical performance.
The intervention will not substantially increase alloy density.
The expected mechanical improvement applies primarily near 1000°C under load.
From room temperature to approximately 600°C, the modified alloy should perform comparably to the baseline.
Approximately 1000°C is representative of jet-turbine operating conditions.
The magnitude of strengthening and optimal oxide concentration and distribution may vary with processing conditions.
Industrial scale-up may introduce additional uncertainty.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits substitution of yttrium with an unspecified alternative oxide-former, but the mediator is specifically Y2O3; an alternative element cannot form Y2O3 in the absence of yttrium.

The prediction allows minimal changes in room-temperature properties, whereas the falsification rule treats any deterioration relative to baseline as falsifying, including a small deterioration that could fall within 'minimal changes.'
